view.label: Critical Miss
view.verdict: You have a stronger UX leadership story than your summary suggests: you manage eight designers and researchers, own the UX budget, and have a measurable product outcome. Opening with “Senior UX Designer” undersells that management scope.

misses.fix: Replace the opening sentence of your summary with a UX design leadership introduction that foregrounds your eight-person team, budget ownership, and product strategy responsibilities.
misses.why: A reviewer hiring a UX design manager needs to see your leadership scope immediately. Your current opening makes them dig into your experience to find it.

Proven track record of managing cross-functional teams and budgets while delivering scalable design solutions that enhance engagement and customer satisfaction. Adept at balancing business goals with user needs to create impactful experiences in fast-paced environments.

view.label: Critical Miss
view.verdict: You have strong evidence of technical leadership and business impact; the repeated “I” openings make your experience read more like a personal narrative than a polished senior-level resume.

misses.fix: Remove the first-person openings throughout Experience, starting with changing “I led” to “Led” in your first OptiMed bullet.
misses.why: Reviewers hiring a senior data scientist or technical lead need to scan quickly for ownership, technical depth, and results. Leading directly with action verbs makes those strengths easier to spot without changing your claims.
